chunk_findings.detail: The cap loop does not actually keep the newest files under the caps. It uses `i` from the original candidate list as the kept-file count and subtracts the size of files it has just deleted, so files deleted for one reason are still counted against the count cap and older files can be retained after newer ones are discarded. For example, with `DDFLOW_INDEX_MAX_FILES=3`, `DDFLOW_INDEX_MAX_MB=10`, current `keep` size 1 MiB, and non-current candidates sorted newest-first as 20 MiB, 1 MiB, 1 MiB, the first 20 MiB file is deleted for exceeding the size cap; the first 1 MiB file is then kept; the second 1 MiB file is deleted because `i + 1` is 3, even though `keep` plus both 1 MiB files would be three files and 3 MiB total, within both caps. A similar size-cap case deletes a newer index while retaining an older one: with cap 100 MiB, `keep` 98 MiB, newer candidate 3 MiB, older candidate 1 MiB, the newer file is deleted and the older file is kept. That contradicts “GC oldest first” and can discard more useful newer indexes while retaining stale older ones.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/store/_fingerprint.py:collect_over_cap

chunk_findings.detail: The cache is bounded only by main `index.db*` files, not by their companion files, and orphan companions are never collected. The loop only processes files whose `_INDEX_FILE` match has an empty `group(2)` (main index files) and deletes `-wal`, `-shm`, and `-lock` companions only while the corresponding main file is present. If a main file is removed but a companion remains, or if one of the companion `unlink()` calls fails and is suppressed, the companion becomes an orphan. On the next GC call it is skipped because it is not a main file, and its size is never included in `total`. For example, a leftover `index.db-abc-wal` with no `index.db-abc` remains forever, so the directory can exceed both the file-count and size caps despite the stated “total size cap” and bounded-derived-cache intent.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/store/_fingerprint.py:collect_over_cap

chunk_findings.detail: Bad numeric environment values are not fully handled. `_env_num` catches only `ValueError` from `float(...)`, but `collect_over_cap` then calls `int(_env_num(...))`. Setting `DDFLOW_INDEX_MAX_FILES=nan` makes `_env_num` return `nan`, and `int(nan)` raises `ValueError`; setting `DDFLOW_INDEX_MAX_FILES=inf` raises `OverflowError`. Similarly, `DDFLOW_INDEX_MAX_MB=nan` makes `total <= max_bytes` always false, causing GC to delete all non-current index files even when the count and intended size caps would allow them. These knobs should fall back to defaults for invalid numeric values rather than crashing or deleting everything.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/store/_fingerprint.py:_env_num

chunk_findings.detail: `monkeypatch.setattr(S, "FOLD_REV", S.FOLD_REV + 1)` patches the re-exported attribute on `ddflow.infra.store`, not necessarily the global used by `code_fingerprint`. The constants-exemption file for this change is `docs/ddflow/constants-exemptions.d/ddflow.infra.store._fingerprint.toml`, and the fingerprint logic lives in `ddflow/infra/store/_fingerprint.py`; if `code_fingerprint` is defined there, its `__globals__` still contains the original `_fingerprint.FOLD_REV`. In that case, after `cache_clear()`, the next `S.code_fingerprint()` call recomputes with the unchanged fold revision, so `assert S.code_fingerprint() != before` fails. The test should patch the module where the function’s globals live, e.g. `S.code_fingerprint.__globals__["FOLD_REV"]`, or import `_fingerprint` and patch that module.

chunk_findings.detail: The GC skips every file whose matched suffix is non-empty and not one of `-wal/-shm/-lock` (`if m.group(2): continue`), but it also does not count those files in `sized`. A rebuild temp file such as `index.db.<hash>.tmp` left by an interrupted rebuild, or any other non-companion suffix, is therefore never removed and never contributes to the file-count or size cap. chunk_findings.detail: The GC loop walks `mains` newest-first and deletes the first file that would exceed the MB cap, then goes on to keep even older files if they fit. chunk_findings.detail: `collect_over_cap` only discovers files with `directory.glob("index.db*")`. The module’s own existing comment describes `index.db` as the **pre-fingerprint** file; the current fingerprint indexes are named after the fingerprint (e.g. `index-<fingerprint>.db`) and therefore do not start with `index.db`. Given a directory containing `index-aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa.db` and `index-bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb.db` with `keep="index-aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa.db"`, this glob returns no names, `mains` is empty, and the function returns `[]`. The new count/size cap therefore never removes real fingerprint index files, so 20 core edits can still leave more than `K` index files, defeating the bug fix.

chunk_findings.detail: The test `test_a_total_size_cap_removes_oldest_first` asserts that `[p.name[9:] for p in _mains(repo)] == [f"{3:016x}"]`, but the indexing expression `p.name[9:]` strips the first 9 characters of the filename. Since an index filename is formatted as `index.db-<hash>`, where `index.db-` has a length of 9, `p.name[9:]` evaluates to just the `<hash>` portion of the filename, which matches `f"{3:016x}"`. However, if `_mains(repo)` returns multiple files or an incorrect file, slicing 9 characters off the prefix when checking against a 16-hex string can lead to an incorrect length or type comparison, and more importantly, `_mains(repo)` returns Path objects whose names are actually compared against the bare hash string while `p.name` is compared directly. Given input where `_mains(repo)` returns `[Path('index.db-0000000000000003')]`, `p.name[9:]` evaluates to `'0000000000000003'`, which matches `f"{3:016x}"`, but if `_mains` returns files with different naming lengths or unexpected paths, this test assertion is brittle and can raise a ValueError or TypeError on string formatting mismatches during test execution.

chunk_findings.detail: The GC skips every file whose matched suffix is non-empty and not one of `-wal/-shm/-lock` (`if m.group(2): continue`), but it also does not count those files in `sized`. A rebuild temp file such as `index.db.<hash>.tmp` left by an interrupted rebuild, or any other non-companion suffix, is therefore never removed and never contributes to the file-count or size cap. Given a directory containing `index.db.keep` plus many `index.db.<hash>.tmp` files from obsolete fingerprints, `collect_over_cap` can return `[]` while the actual number and total size of `index.db*` derived files grow without bound, defeating the stated “at most K files plus total size cap” / bounded derived-cache behavior.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/store/_fingerprint.py:collect_over_cap

chunk_findings.detail: This change introduces new environment knobs (`DDFLOW_INDEX_KEY`, `DDFLOW_INDEX_GC`, `DDFLOW_INDEX_MAX_FILES`, `DDFLOW_INDEX_MAX_MB`) by reading `os.environ` directly in the store module. Under the project guidance, environment access is an external dependency that should go through the adapter port, so this violates [r-adapters].
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/store/_fingerprint.py:os.environ

chunk_findings.detail: `test_the_newest_files_survive_and_oldest_go` only sets `DDFLOW_INDEX_MAX_FILES` and does not clear the kill-switch variable `DDFLOW_INDEX_GC`. `monkeypatch.setenv` preserves other existing environment variables, so if the environment already contains `DDFLOW_INDEX_GC=0` (the documented kill switch), GC is disabled for the test. `_simulate_edits(log, repo, cfg, 6)` then leaves six main index files, while the assertion expects exactly the two newest files `[f"{4:016x}", f"{5:016x}"]`, so the test fails purely because of ambient environment state.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_index_file_cap.py:48

chunk_findings.detail: `test_a_bad_cap_value_falls_back_and_orphans_go` also does not clear `DDFLOW_INDEX_GC`. If the ambient environment has `DDFLOW_INDEX_GC=0`, the kill switch disables GC before the bad-cap fallback is exercised. In that case `_simulate_edits(log, repo, cfg, 4)` leaves four main index files and the orphan `index.db-eeee...-wal` sidecar remains, causing both `assert 1 <= len(_mains(repo)) <= 3` and `assert not orphan.exists()` to fail.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_index_file_cap.py:96

chunk_findings.detail: The GC loop walks `mains` newest-first and deletes the first file that would exceed the MB cap, then goes on to keep even older files if they fit. Input: `DDFLOW_INDEX_MAX_MB=1`, `DDFLOW_INDEX_MAX_FILES=10`, a 921600-byte `keep`, a newer 204800-byte `index.db-new`, and an older 102400-byte `index.db-old`. `collect_over_cap` deletes `index.db-new` because 921600+204800 > 1048576, then keeps `index.db-old` because 921600+102400 <= 1048576. That leaves the oldest file while deleting a newer one, contrary to the change’s stated “GC oldest first” behavior.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/store/_fingerprint.py:collect_over_cap

chunk_findings.detail: Direct `os.environ.get` reads for `DDFLOW_INDEX_KEY`, `DDFLOW_INDEX_GC`, `DDFLOW_INDEX_MAX_FILES`, and `DDFLOW_INDEX_MAX_MB` bypass `ddflow/adapters`. [r-adapters] says every external dependency, including the environment, must go through a port in `ddflow/adapters`; this change uses `os.environ` directly, so an env port/fake cannot be swapped and the dependency is not isolated in its own adapter file.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/store/_fingerprint.py:_fingerprint,collect_over_cap

chunk_findings.detail: The change alters observable cache lifecycle behavior: index files are now capped by count/size and the index key changes to an explicit SCHEMA/FOLD_REV, so users upgrading can expect old index files to be garbage-collected/rebuild. The whole-change manifest lists only `docs/ddflow/constants-exemptions.d/ddflow.infra.store._fingerprint.toml` as documentation and contains no upgrade note, violating the stated requirement that an upgrade note ships with the change. This is a documentation defect for a behavior change.
chunk_findings.title: (manifest) [r-docs-with-the-change]

chunk_findings.detail: The test rebinds `S.FOLD_REV` on the `ddflow.infra.store` package namespace, but `code_fingerprint` is defined in `ddflow.infra.store._fingerprint` and merely re-exported through `S`. Rebinding the package attribute does not rebind the `_fingerprint.FOLD_REV` global that `code_fingerprint` reads, so `assert S.code_fingerprint() != before` fails even when the implementation is correct. The test must monkeypatch the defining module (e.g. `ddflow.infra.store._fingerprint.FOLD_REV`), not the re-export.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_index_file_cap.py:test_the_key_ignores_source_edits_but_follows_fold_rev

chunk_findings.detail: The test claims to verify “removes oldest first” under the size cap but only asserts `len(_mains(repo)) <= 2`. With the test’s own cap of 1.5 file sizes and four equal-size files, a broken implementation that deletes the newest file first still leaves one file and passes. To satisfy the stated GC-oldest-first behavior, the test should assert the single surviving suffix is `f"{3:016x}"` (the newest file), not just an upper bound.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_index_file_cap.py:test_a_total_size_cap_removes_oldest_first

chunk_findings.detail: These tests set some `DDFLOW_INDEX_*` variables but do not clear inherited `DDFLOW_INDEX_GC` / `DDFLOW_INDEX_MAX_MB` before running. If pytest runs with `DDFLOW_INDEX_GC=0` already set in the environment, `test_the_newest_files_survive_and_oldest_go` keeps all six files and fails against the expected `[f"{4:016x}", f"{5:016x}"]`; likewise `test_a_bad_cap_value_falls_back_and_orphans_go` sees no GC and has more than 3 files. These tests need to `monkeypatch.delenv` the relevant env vars, as `test_twenty_core_edits_leave_at_most_k_index_files` already does.

Given a directory containing `index.db.keep` plus many abandoned `index.db.<hash>.tmp` files left by interrupted rebuilds, those tmp files are never removed and never count toward file-count or size caps, so the bounded-cache guarantee is still violated.

chunk_findings.detail: This test is not changed by the diff and still rebinds `S.FOLD_REV`, which is a package-level name re-exported by `ddflow.infra.store`. `code_fingerprint` actually lives in `ddflow.infra.store._fingerprint` and reads that module’s `FOLD_REV` global, not `S.FOLD_REV`’s attribute. As a result `S.code_fingerprint()` keeps returning the old value and `assert S.code_fingerprint() != before` fails even when the implementation is correct.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_index_file_cap.py:test_the_key_ignores_source_edits_but_follows_fold_rev

chunk_findings.detail: The test `test_a_total_size_cap_removes_oldest_first` asserts that `[p.name[9:] for p in _mains(repo)] == [f"{3:016x}"]`, but the indexing expression `p.name[9:]` strips the first 9 characters of the filename. Since an index filename is formatted as `index.db-<hash>`, where `index.db-` has a length of 9, `p.name[9:]` evaluates to just the `<hash>` portion of the filename, which matches `f"{3:016x}"`. However, if `_mains(repo)` returns multiple files or an incorrect file, slicing 9 characters off the prefix when checking against a 16-hex string can lead to an incorrect length or type comparison, and more importantly, `_mains(repo)` returns Path objects whose names are actually compared against the bare hash string while `p.name` is compared directly. Given input where `_mains(repo)` returns `[Path('index.db-0000000000000003')]`, `p.name[9:]` evaluates to `'0000000000000003'`, which matches `f"{3:016x}"`, but if `_mains` returns files with different naming lengths or unexpected paths, this test assertion is brittle and can raise a ValueError or TypeError on string formatting mismatches during test execution.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_index_file_cap.py:75

chunk_findings.detail: `collect_over_cap` only discovers files with `directory.glob("index.db*")`. The module’s own existing comment describes `index.db` as the **pre-fingerprint** file; the current fingerprint indexes are named after the fingerprint (e.g. `index-<fingerprint>.db`) and therefore do not start with `index.db`. Given a directory containing `index-aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa.db` and `index-bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb.db` with `keep="index-aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa.db"`, this glob returns no names, `mains` is empty, and the function returns `[]`. The new count/size cap therefore never removes real fingerprint index files, so 20 core edits can still leave more than `K` index files, defeating the bug fix.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/store/_fingerprint.py:collect_over_cap

chunk_findings.detail: The new fingerprint-key branch and `collect_over_cap` directly read `os.environ` and directly access the filesystem (`Path.glob`, `Path.stat`, `Path.unlink`, `Path.with_name`) instead of going through a `ddflow/adapters` port, violating [r-adapters]. This makes the environment/filesystem behavior inaccessible to port fakes and hard to swap single-place, which is exactly what the rule requires.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/store/_fingerprint.py

chunk_findings.detail: [r-adapters] The new `_env_num` helper owns environment lookup for the new `DDFLOW_INDEX_MAX_FILES` / `DDFLOW_INDEX_MAX_MB` knobs, and the same change adds filesystem helpers (`sized`, `remove`, `collect_over_cap`) directly in `ddflow/infra/store/_fingerprint.py`. Rule r-adapters requires environment and filesystem-layout dependencies to go through a single port under `ddflow/adapters`; this change adds direct process-environment/disk access in store code with no adapter file, so those behaviors cannot be isolated, faked, or swapped without touching the real environment and filesystem.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/store/_fingerprint.py:_env_num

chunk_findings.detail: The test never simulates a source edit. It computes `S.code_fingerprint()`, bumps `S.FOLD_REV`, and only asserts the value changed. An implementation that still hashes the source tree into the fingerprint (so every developer source edit changes the key) and simply also includes `FOLD_REV` would pass this test, leaving the exact “not the source hash” part of the change unfalsified.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_index_file_cap.py:test_the_key_ignores_source_edits_but_follows_fold_rev

chunk_findings.detail: The assertion is only `S.code_fingerprint() != explicit`. If `DDFLOW_INDEX_KEY=source` returned a constant, an empty string, or explicit plus a salt, the test would still pass. It therefore does not verify that source mode actually restores the previous source-hash behavior, so a broken source mode would go undetected here.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_index_file_cap.py:test_source_key_mode_restores_the_source_hash

chunk_findings.detail: The modified cleanup path still performs filesystem operations directly in store code: it operates on filesystem `Path` objects from `mains`, obtains sizes with `sized(directory / keep)`, and deletes files with `remove(f)`. This same function is now re-exported in `ddflow/infra/store/__init__.py`, and this delta adds no adapter port under `ddflow/adapters` for the bounded-cache behavior. That leaves the new cache-bounding logic outside the boundary required by [r-adapters], so the prior untriaged filesystem-port violation still holds for the visible change.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/store/_fingerprint.py:collect_over_cap
